subject: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@searchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps:

Recap:
- Goal: improve semantic search relevance for product docs and support articles, reduce false positives from recent category drift.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + custom text preprocessing, 1.2M documents, typical query lengths ~10–30 tokens.
- Success signals: higher Recall@10 and improvement in human-rated relevance on top-5 results; stable dimensionality and index size limits for cost predictability.

What we propose for validation:
- Run a short fit validation using your 1k sample (attached) and our embedding candidates: 1536-d open model (recommended baseline) and a 768-d cost-optimized variant.
- Metrics we'll report: Recall@1/5/10, MRR, cosine similarity distribution, cluster drift score vs historical snapshot.
- Deliverables: embed_eval_report_v1.pdf, sample prompt set (CSV), and a short notebook with eval scripts.

Attachments: embed_eval_report_v1.pdf (example), sample_prompt_set.csv, searchly_sample_1k.jsonl

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you’re OK with us ingesting the attached sample for evaluation (we only use it for ephemeral evaluation and delete after).
2) If yes, we’ll run the validation and share a result deck + a recommended model and config (quantization, dimensionality, batching).
3) Schedule a 30-min review next week to walk through results.

Open questions from our call for the evaluation run:
- Are there any sensitive fields in the sample that need tokenization/PII handling?
- Target latency SLOs for vector search at 99th perc? (helps us recommend dimensionality/batching)

Happy to discuss — proposed times for the review: Tue 12/1 10am or Wed 12/2 3pm PT.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Thanks Marcus — quick answers and a couple of asks.

We’re good with you using the 1k sample for the evaluation. No PII in that sample; it’s been sanitized. Our main concerns:
- Drift: over the last 6 months many docs shifted from technical to business language and we’ve seen a drop in relevance for search queries related to config/how-to.
- Dimensionality vs cost: our infra cost is sensitive — 1536d looks ideal for quality, but we need to understand the cost delta for index size and latency.

Questions:
1) For the metrics you listed, can you include a simple human-grade rubric (3 raters, binary relevance) so we can map metrics to business outcomes?
2) Can you provide a quick estimate of tokenization / ingest cost for the 1.2M corpus if we were to reindex at 1536d?

We’re available for the Tue 12/1 10am slot. Please send an invite.

—Samir
Director of Search Engineering
Searchly Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@searchly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Samir — great notes. Short answers inline and a proposed evaluation plan.

1) Human-grade rubric: yes — we’ll run a 3-rater binary relevance test on a stratified sample (200 queries) and include agreement stats (Fleiss’ kappa). That will let us translate Recall / MRR improvements to % of sessions with better top-5 hits.

2) Reindex cost estimate (ballpark): for 1.2M docs at 1536 dims: index size ~1.8–2.1 TB (dense vectors + metadata), one-time tokenization + embed compute ~6–8 GPU-hours on T4-equivalent for a batched run, approximate cloud cost $1.8k–$3k depending on concurrency. For 768 dims expect ~45% smaller index and ~40% less compute time. We’ll run a more precise estimate once we have a sample of doc length distribution.

Recommended candidate models for validation:
- redwood-embed-1536-v1 (baseline): higher recall/robustness to drift, recommended default for product docs.
- redwood-embed-768-v1 (cost-optimized): lower memory, slightly lower recall but often similar MRR for shorter queries.

Evaluation plan we’ll run today:
- Compute embeddings for both dims on your 1k sample.
- Metrics: Recall@1/5/10, MRR, average cosine similarity for positives vs random negatives, cluster centroid shift vs your historical snapshot.
- Dimensionality check: measure nearest-neighbor distance scaling and compression sensitivity.

I attached an example eval report (embed_eval_report_v1.pdf) and the sample prompt set. Also linking our benchmark doc: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/embeddings-benchmarks-1536-vs-768

We’ll proceed with the run and aim to share results before the Tue 12/1 10am meeting. I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-30T13:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Embeddings fit validation follow-up / next steps

Looping in a couple of infra/ops notes for the eval run:
- Use 16-bit quantized float path for the 1536 run only if we see >2x memory pressure; otherwise run full fp32 to avoid small-quality deltas in neighborhood structure.
- Enable prefix KV caching during batched embed generation to speed up embed compute for similar documents.
- For the index: recommend a single shard of Faiss HNSW for this 1k test, but note we should simulate production shard counts when reporting latency.

I’ll take lead on the evaluation notebook and sanity checks. Rishi — can you prepare the quick cost delta table (768 vs 1536) and drop it into the shared drive?

Marissa
